name: Gold
hook: The metal behind the rushes, the legends and Fort Knox — and Jeopardy never stops digging it up.

facts.label: Au
facts.statement: Gold is a precious metal and chemical element with the symbol Au. Pure gold is 24 karats, and electrum is mostly gold with at least 20 percent silver.

facts.label: El Dorado
facts.statement: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold sought in vain by conquistadors including Pizarro and Sir Walter Raleigh, who searched in what is now Guyana.

facts.label: Fort Knox
facts.statement: Fort Knox in Kentucky is the site of the U.S. Gold Bullion Depository; in December 1941 the Declaration of Independence was sent there for safekeeping.

facts.label: California Gold Rush
facts.statement: Gold discovered in California in 1848 gave the state its "Golden State" nickname and produced Gold Country towns such as Rough & Ready and Fiddletown.

facts.label: the Klondike
facts.statement: The Klondike gold rush began after gold was found near Bonanza Creek in the Yukon in 1896; Whitehorse grew as a transit hub to the fields.

facts.label: South Africa
facts.statement: Gold from the Witwatersrand in the Transvaal makes South Africa one of the world's top gold producers, and mines like Savuka and Driefontein are among the deepest.

facts.label: Denver
facts.statement: The 1859 Pikes Peak gold rush created Denver, which merged with Auraria in 1860.
